description: The spec for the workshop's own agent harness. The client practices what the workshop teaches: these requirements are the source of truth, the tagged Cucumber scenarios are their executable form, and SpecCompletenessTest fails the build if the two drift apart.

requirements.title: The agent narrates the MCP handshake
requirements.story: As a workshop attendee, I want the agent to narrate the initialize handshake so that I can see how a host learns a server's identity and workflow instructions.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a server that identifies itself, when the walkthrough runs, then the narration names the server and its version
Given a server that provides workflow instructions, when the walkthrough runs, then the instructions are narrated indented as quoted server output
Given a server with no instructions, when the walkthrough runs, then no instructions block is narrated

requirements.title: The agent discovers and narrates the server's tools
requirements.story: As a workshop attendee, I want the agent to list every discovered tool with a one-line summary so that I can see discovery replace hardcoding.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a server exposing tools, when the walkthrough runs, then each tool is narrated with its name and the first sentence of its description
Given a tool whose description has no sentence break, when the walkthrough runs, then the full description is narrated unchanged

requirements.title: The agent establishes the baseline bar color
requirements.story: As a workshop attendee, I want the agent to run the kata suite through run_tests and announce the bar color so that the feedback loop is visible before any work starts.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a baseline run_tests result with phase GREEN, when the walkthrough runs, then the narration reports the bar is GREEN

requirements.title: The agent picks the next pending requirement from the spec
requirements.story: As a workshop attendee, I want the agent to select the first pending requirement and fetch its detail so that the handoff names concrete next work.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a backlog with a pending requirement, when the walkthrough runs, then the agent fetches that requirement's detail and names it in the handoff
Given a backlog with no pending requirements, when the walkthrough runs, then the detail step is skipped and the handoff uses a placeholder

requirements.title: The agent surfaces tool errors instead of hiding them
requirements.story: As a workshop attendee, I want error results flagged in the narration so that I can see agents read failures and recover from them.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a tool call whose result has isError true, when the walkthrough narrates it, then the narration flags the result with isError=true

requirements.title: The agent always closes the server connection
requirements.story: As a workshop attendee, I want the client connection closed when the walkthrough finishes or fails so that no orphaned server process is left behind.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a walkthrough that completes, when the run returns, then the connection has been closed
Given a walkthrough that fails mid-run with an error, when the failure propagates, then the connection has still been closed

requirements.title: The client launches the bdd binary as the MCP server
requirements.story: As a workshop attendee, I want the Java client to start bdd mcp serve so that the walkthrough talks to the same server Cursor uses.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a workshop root and a bdd binary, when ServerLaunch.bdd is built, then the program is that binary and the args are mcp serve --root <root>

requirements.title: Discovery carries each tool's input schema and required arguments
requirements.story: As a workshop attendee, I want discovered tools to keep their JSON Schema so that a client can call tools it did not hard-code.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a tool whose schema requires id, when required arguments are read, then id is listed

requirements.title: The tool plan names exactly the 23 served tools
requirements.story: As a maintainer, I want a 24th MCP tool to fail the Java build until it is planned so that the client cannot silently skip new surface area.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the ToolPlan, when it is listed, then it names exactly 23 tools
Given a discovered tool that is not in the plan, when the sweep runs, then that tool is reported as unexpected

requirements.title: A read-only sweep calls every planned read tool and skips mutations
requirements.story: As a workshop attendee, I want a default sweep that does not stage files so that I can prove discovery without mutating the kata.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a server that exposes every planned tool, when a read-only sweep runs, then staging and gated tools are not called

requirements.title: Gated tool refusals are expected, not sweep failures
requirements.story: As a workshop attendee, I want start_refactor off GREEN to count as a successful gated call so that the sweep can exercise refusals.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a gated tool that answers with isError, when a mutating sweep runs, then the call is recorded and is not a failure
